tableCard.relationshipsExplainer: A relationship (foreign key) links a row in one table to a row in another — it's how the database keeps connected data consistent. For example, an <1>orders</1> table can have a <3>customer_id</3> column that points to the <5>customers</5> table: the database then guarantees every order always points to a customer that actually exists. The <7>On Delete</7> option controls what happens when that customer is deleted — <9>Cascade</9> deletes their orders too, <11>Restrict</11> blocks the deletion while orders exist, and <13>Set Null</13> just clears the link, keeping the orders. Use relationships whenever one thing "belongs to" another — a comment belongs to a post, an order belongs to a customer — instead of duplicating that data in every row.
tableCard.indexExplainer: An index is like a book's index: instead of the database reading record by record to find what you asked for, it jumps straight to the right spot. Add an index to any column you frequently use to <1>search</1> or <3>filter</3> data — for example, an index on <5>email</5> if your app looks up customers by email, or a composite index on <7>org_id + status</7> if you always list an organization's orders filtered by status. Check <9>Unique</9> when that value (or combination of values) must never repeat, like a national ID or a coupon code — the database then enforces no duplicates on its own. Without an index, searches on large tables get slower and slower as data grows.
